  (1)  LOCATION:  850 EAST GLENOAKS BOULEVARD

  ~  VARIANCE CASE NO. PVAR 1824584

  APPLICANT:  Shoghig Yepremian - Yepremian Consulting, Inc.

  ZONE :  "R1" - (Low Density Residential) Zone, Floor Area District II

  STAFF:  Brad Collin, Senior Planner

  LEGAL DESCRIPTION: Lot 55 in Bellehurst Park Tract

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION
  An application for a Standards Variance to maintain an existing nonconforming
  driveway width of seven feet, five inches, where nine feet is required in
  conjunction with an addition of approximately 492 square feet to an existing
  1, 126 square-foot single family dwelling.

  CODE REQUIRES
  Standards Variance
  (1) Minimum nine-foot driveway width.

  APPLICANT'S PROPOSAL
  Standards Variance
  (1) To construct a 492 square-foot addition while maintaining an existing non-
  conforming driveway width of seven feet, five inches.

  2
 Planning Commission Minutes
August 2 1, 20 19

  ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  The project is exempt from environmental review as a Class 1 "Existing Facility"
  exemption (Section 15301 (e) (1) of the State CEQA Guidelines) because this
  application is for the maintenance of an existing nonconforming driveway width in
  conjunction with a 492 square-foot addition (190 square feet at the front and 302
  square feet at the rear).

  STAFF
  Staff member Brad Collin, case planner on the case, presented the staff report.
  He stated that this item on the agenda is an appeal of Planning Hearing Officer's
  denial of Variance Case No. PVAR1824584 to allow the maintenance of a
  nonconforming driveway width of seven feet, five inches where nine feet is
  required in conjunction with an addition of approximately 492 square feet to an
  existing 1,126 square-foot single family dwelling. He answered questions from the
  Planning Commissioners.

  Mr. Collin stated that the Community Development Department staff recommends
  that the Planning Commission sustain the Planning Hearing Officer's decision to
  deny Variance Case No. PVAR1824584, located at 850 East Glenoaks
  Boulevard , as stated in the staff report dated August 21, 2019.

  APPELLANTS ARE THE SAME AS THE APPLICANTS
  ~  Ms. Shoghig Yepremian, consultant on the project presented the case. She
  stated that the subject site is a 7,240 square foot rectangular lot with a 1,126 square
  foot, one-story, and three-bedroom single-family reside·nce. The lot has frontage on
  East Glenoaks Boulevard and is fairly flat. The house was built in 1947 with the
  current driveway width of 7 feet, 5 inches. The project is currently under construction
  with the additions to the front and rear, a portion of which is adjacent to the subject
  driveway. This also includes 220 square feet addition of living area that was built
  without permits and is being legalized as part of the building permit.

  Ms. Yepremian referred to Zoning Code Sections:
  - 30.32.130 (C) in "R 1" Residential Zone as it relates to existing non-conforming
  driveways,
  - 30.32.130 (C) relating to Driveway standards, and
  - 30.44020(J) relating to Administrative Exception.

  Ms. Yepremian stated that the:
  Planning Hearing Officer arbitrarily made the decision to apply the 9-foot
  driveway width requirement on the addition portion of the house when the
  existing nonconforming driveway width has been 7 feet, 5 inches, for 72 years.
  Planning staff recommended that the property owner to apply for a Standards
  Variance application knowing that there is an Administrative Exception review
  process in place as per Zoning Code Section 30.44020(J).
  Other City departments did not have any concerns or comments regarding the
  Variance application.

  3
 Planning Commission Minutes
August 2 1, 2019

  Ms. Yepremian pointed out that a Building Permit was issued By Building and
  Safety Section, for the proposed additions after a detailed plan check review
  process. Due to an error in calculation, the plans showed an 8-foot wide
  driveway instead of 7 feet, 5 inches. The plans were approved by Building and
  Safety section staff, with an 8-foot wide driveway, and a site inspection was also
  conducted.

  Ms. Yepremian apprised the Planning Commissioners that after a complaint was made
  by an anonymous person ; the plans were modified to reflect the correct measurement
  of 7 feet , 5 inches.

  Ms. Yepremian stated that at this point, staff required the owner to file for an
  Administrative Exception to allow a driveway width of less than 8 feet. The
  Administrative Exception application was filed by the owner, and then later on
  was withdrawn. Planning staff recommended that a new Standards Variance
  application to be filed and to be heard by a Planning Hearing Officer.

  ~  Mr. Nareg Khodadadi, architect on the project, presented the case. He stated
  that an Administrative Exception was submitted to maintain the 7-foot, 5-inch driveway
  width where 9 feet is required for the existing house, but was withdrawn. As per
  Planning Division staff's recommendation, a new application was filed for a Variance to
  maintain the 7-foot, 5-inch driveway width for both the house and the proposed
  additions.
  WRITTEN COMMUNICATION
  IN FAVOR
  - Petition signed by thirteen (1 3) neighbors

  IN OPPOSITION:  None.
  INTERESTED PARTY:  None.

  SPEAKING AT THE HEARING

  IN FAVOR
  Armond Eisavians
  Roobina lsavians - owner
  Hamlet Malek Stepanians
  Aden Malek Stepanians
  0 . Osayan - General Contractor

  INTERESTED PARTY:  No one.
  IN OPPOSITION:  No one.

  4
 Planning Commission Minutes
August 21, 2019

  REBUTTAL
  Appellant is the same as the Applicant
  ~ Ms. Yepremian stated that:
  Staff failed to review this project as a minor addition to a single family house
  with an existing non-conforming driveway. Instead applied a 9-foor wide
  driveway standard to the addition portion of the house when the Zoning Code
  Section 30.32.130 (C) allows an 8-foot wide or less driveway width for house
  additions.
  This project should have been reviewed as an "Administrative Exception" - It
  is a legal non-conforming house and a legal non-conforming driveway.
  Non-conforming driveways less than eight (8) feet in width on properties with
  an existing single family residential use where an addition to the building, or
  expanded or new garage is proposed may maintain a width less than eight
  (8) feet, as long as the non-conformity regarding driveway width is not
  increased, and the driveway can reasonably provide access to the garage.
  This property is unique because it is next to a wash.
  There was no concern or opposition from the neighborhood residents regarding
  this Variance application.
  Thirteen neighbors have signed a petition in support of the project.

  DISCUSSION BY PLANNING COMMISSIONERS
  Planning Commissioners discussed the following:
  -- Survey prior to submitting the project for Building and Safety's plan check review.
  -- Time limits.
  -- Consideration of an Administrative Exception application - why did planning staff
  reject the application
  -- Plans approved by City staff by mistake.
  -- Plans submitted by the applicant with incorrect measurements
  -- City staff and the applicant both are at fault.
  -- Code 30.44.020 (J) was discussed
  -- The proposed project is built and completed but final approval has not been given
  by the City.

  It was the consensus of all the Planning Commissioners that this project was
  permitted initially and building permits were issued accordingly, and the applicant
  proceeded with the approved plans and built it. However, an error was made by both
  the City staff and the applicant.

  Upon questioning by the Planning Commissioners, Mr. Collin informed them that:
  -- The error was detected after a complaint was made by a neighbor.
  -- To allow this driveway width will be precedent setting and should not be
  encouraged due to difficulties created by not being able to access detached
  garages at the rear of the properties.
  -- All required findings could not be met, therefore the Planning Hearing Officer
  denied the variance request to maintain the existing nonconforming driveway
  width of 7 feet, 5 inches.

  5
 Planning Commission Minutes
August 21, 20 19

  Planning Commissioners further discussed the appeal and made the following motion.

  MOTION
  Moved by Planning Commissioner Astorian , seconded by Planning Commissioner
  Chraghchian , that upon review and consideration of Variance Case No. PVAR
  1824584, located at 850 East Glenoaks Boulevard , and after having conducted
  and closed a public hearing on said variance case, the Planning Commission
  hereby continues the agenda item to September 4, 2019 for the preparation of
  findings to support reversing the Planning Hearing Officer's decision to deny the
  application made in connection Variance Case No. PVAR 1824584.
  VOTE
  Ayes:  Astorian, Chraghchian, Minassian
  Noes:  Shahbazian
  Abstain:  None
